title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - streaming stability, functions & structured output
author: Emma Liu
description: Goal: Bring Redwood's /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer to parity with OpenAI for parameters, roles, stop/logprobs exposure, streaming stability, function/tool calling behavior, and response formatting. Motivation: downstream customers use the OpenAI-compatible endpoint for migration; parity reduces edge-case differences that cause production regressions. This PR implements stable streaming framing (fixing partial-chunk reassembly and SSE keepalive), deterministic function call selection/formatting, explicit role handling for assistant/system/user, pass-through of stop sequences and logprobs (when requested), and structured-output helpers to ensure JSON/tool outputs are preserved across streaming and non-streaming flows. Work done (high level): 1) Streaming: replace ad-hoc chunker with new streaming-sink that buffers tokens at sentence/JSON-boundary heuristics and emits stable SSE events; add per-connection backpressure metrics and unit tests that simulate chunk splits across boundaries. 2) Functions/tool-calls: align function-call selection logic with OpenAI semantics: when a function is returned by the model we return a single assistant message with content=null and function_call.payload set; when multiple candidate function calls appear we prefer deterministic first-pass based on model score then fallback to heuristic. 3) Roles & stop/logprobs: ensure role tokens are recorded and returned in token-level outputs; implement sanitized stop sequence handling upstream so users get identical stopping behavior; expose logprobs for text completions and chat when model supports it. 4) Response formatting: add structured-output transport that preserves raw model JSON across streaming boundaries and reconstructs for non-streaming responses; add tests for nested JSON and tool-call payloads. 5) Backwards compatibility: changes are additive at the API level; default behavior unchanged unless client requests functions/logprobs or uses streaming. Migration notes: clients should not need changes for standard chat usage. Clients relying on exact SSE chunk boundaries should switch to reassembly logic provided in SDKs (PATCH included). CI: fixes flakey streaming integration tests and adds a stress test that simulates 200 concurrent streaming clients. Checklist: - [x] Add compatibility behavior and tests. - [x] SDK patches (Python/TS) to handle reassembly. - [x] Documentation updates (compat guide and release notes). Related: linear/ENG-1245 for streaming stability, ENG-1302 for functions parity.
